title: GL Endo-Parameters
body_html:
GL Endo-Parameters

For an endo-class $\mathfrak c\in\mathscr E(F)$, the draft defines a monoid $\operatorname{vect}(\mathfrak c)$ whose elements are equivalence classes $[\beta,V]$, where $\beta$ supports a ps-character in $\mathfrak c$ and $V$ is a finite-dimensional $F[\beta]$-vector space. The equivalence relation uses similarity of based extensions and equality of $F[\beta]$-dimension.

A $\operatorname{GL}$-endo-parameter over $F$ is a finitely supported section of

$$ \bigsqcup_{\mathfrak c\in\mathscr E(F)} \operatorname{vect}(\mathfrak c) \longrightarrow \mathscr E(F). $$

The set of such parameters is denoted $\mathscr{EP}(F)$. Its degree is

$$ \deg(f)= \sum_{\mathfrak c\in\mathscr E(F)} \dim_F(f(\mathfrak c)). $$

The subset of degree $N$ parameters is denoted $\mathscr{EP}_N(F)$.

The totally positive part $\mathscr{EP}^+(F)$ consists of parameters supported on $\mathscr E^+(F)$, i.e. away from the trivial endo-class. Restricting away from the trivial endo-class gives the depth-positive part of a parameter.

Draft Caution

The draft says one may think of a $\operatorname{GL}$-endo-parameter as a function $\mathscr E(F)\to\mathbb Z_{\ge 0}$, but this loses the bundle/fiber language needed later for classical groups.
